Add Two Numbers (digits stored in reverse order)

Grade-school addition with a carry. Keeping carry != 0 in the loop condition handles a final extra digit (99 + 1). O(max(m, n)). If digits are stored most-significant first, push both lists onto stacks (or reverse them) first.
Reorder List (L0 → Ln → L1 → Ln-1 …)
Combines three building blocks interviewers love: find middle, reverse, merge. O(n) time, O(1) space. Remember to cut the list at the middle (slow.next = null) or you create a cycle.
Copy List with Random Pointer (deep copy)

The map from original to clone lets you wire random pointers that point forward or backward. O(n) time and space. The O(1)-space version interleaves clones (A → A' → B → B'), sets A'.random = A.random.next, then splits the two lists. The same "old → new map" idea solves Clone Graph.
Reverse Nodes in k-Group
Check that k nodes exist, reverse them with prev starting at the node after the group (so the reversed tail already links forward), then reattach. O(n) time, O(1) space.
Sort List in O(n log n) (merge sort on a linked list)

Merge sort suits linked lists: no random access is needed and merging needs no extra array. O(n log n) time, O(log n) recursion stack (bottom-up merge sort makes it O(1)). Quick sort is a poor fit because partitioning needs random access.
Remove Duplicates from a Sorted List (keep one / remove all)
Version I just skips equal neighbours. Version II needs a dummy head because the first node itself may be removed. Both are O(n) time, O(1) space.
Cycle detection: Floyd's slow/fast pointers vs HashSet of visited nodes

| HashSet<ListNode> | Floyd (tortoise and hare)
Time | O(n) average | O(n)
Extra space | O(n) | O(1)
Finds cycle start | Yes: first node already in the set | Yes: reset one pointer to head, move both one step
Code risk | Low | Null checks on fast and fast.next
Rule of thumb: mention the set as the first idea, then give Floyd when the interviewer asks for O(1) space (they almost always do).
Iterative vs recursive linked-list reversal

| Iterative (prev, curr, next) | Recursive
Time | O(n) | O(n)
Extra space | O(1) | O(n) call stack
Long list (105+ nodes) | Safe | Can throw StackOverflowError
Key line | curr.next = prev | head.next.next = head; head.next = null
Useful for | Production code, k-group reversal | Showing recursion skills; reverse from the end
Interview tip: write the iterative version by default and explain why: constant space and no stack-depth risk.
Dummy (sentinel) head vs handling the head as a special case

| Special-case the head | Dummy node before head
Deleting the first node | Separate if branch | Same code as any other node
Building a new list (merge) | Need to pick the first node first | Just append to tail
Return value | head (may have changed) | dummy.next
Extra space | None | One node, O(1)
Rule of thumb: whenever the head itself might be removed or replaced, start with a dummy node.
Two passes (count the length) vs one pass (two pointers with a gap)

Task | Two-pass approach | One-pass approach
Middle node | Count n, walk n/2 | Slow moves 1, fast moves 2
Nth from the end | Count n, walk n - N | Move fast N ahead, then move both
Intersection of two lists | Count both lengths, skip the difference | Each pointer switches to the other list's head at the end
Complexity | O(n) time, O(1) space | O(n) time, O(1) space
Interview tip: both are O(n); the one-pass version is what interviewers expect to see. Know which middle you get for even length: with fast = head and while (fast != null && fast.next != null), slow stops at the second middle.
